title: Ten-day retreats
hookLine: hand in your phone, stop talking, sit: S. N. Goenka's silent ten-day courses

lines: NO TALKING, NO GESTURES, NO EYE CONTACT.
cards: Hand in your phone at the door. Your books and notebook too. From this evening on, no talking to the other students.
No texting, no gestures, not even catching someone's eye across the dining hall. Wake before dawn. Sit.
Eat simply. Sit. A recorded talk in the evening.
Sleep. Then again, for ten days. That's the shape of the silent courses taught by S.

teach.b: The last two days were calm and insight, samatha and vipassana. Goenka's course is built to walk through both, in order. First, the silence.

It's called noble silence: silence of speech and of body, held among the students for nearly the whole course. A student can still speak with the teacher about practice, or with staff about practical needs.
The point isn't punishment. Without talk, the mind has nowhere to hide, and the meditation gets the attention conversation usually takes.
Students also agree to keep basic moral precepts during the course, like not killing and not stealing; tomorrow says more about those.

teach.h: CALM FIRST: THE BREATH AT THE NOSE.
teach.b: Second, calm first. The early days are spent on the breath alone, watched at a small area around the nose: yesterday's practice, narrowed and repeated until the mind steadies. Third, then insight.

teach.h: THEN INSIGHT: SENSATIONS, PART BY PART.
teach.b: Students move attention through the body, part by part, observing sensations and how they change, without craving the pleasant ones or pushing away the unpleasant ones. That's watch it change, practiced at length.

teach.h: NO FEE: CARRIED BY PAST STUDENTS.
teach.b: Near the end, the silence lifts, and students learn a practice of goodwill toward all beings. Fourth, how it's offered. In Goenka's tradition, the courses charge no fee.

Food and lodging are covered by donations from students who've already finished a course and want others to have the chance. So the person beside you in silence was carried there, in part, by strangers who sat before.
Not everyone who hears about this wants to try it, and imagining it is a practice too.

how: Students on Goenka-style courses live at a center for ten days in noble silence, keep basic precepts, practice breath meditation and then vipassana body scanning for long stretches each day, and the courses run on donations from past students.

o: paid wellness getaways with daily yoga and spa time
a monk's ordination, ten days to take lifelong vows
Goenka's silent courses: calm, then insight, with no fee

games.q: it's the third day of a ten-day course, and you badly want to tell the person next to you about a dream. what does noble silence ask?
o: keep it to yourself, and take it back to the cushion.
games.why: noble silence covers speech and body: no talk, no gestures, no notes among students. the mind has nowhere to hide, and that's the point.

practice: Walk yourself through the first morning: the phone gone, nobody to talk to, a bell before dawn, a cushion, the breath at the nose.

Notice what comes up, relief, dread, curiosity, a list of everyone who'd need to know where you were, without deciding anything. Then rest on the breath at the nose, as if this were the first sitting of day one.

wordCard.voice: Ten-day retreats. S. N. Goenka's silent vipassana courses: calm on the breath first, then insight into sensations, offered without a fee. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: ten silent days. Calm first, then insight, all held in noble silence. Until tomorrow.
